- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Adds the `dataset` section to `PretrainConfigContainer`: a declarative `GPTDatasetConfig` (plus `DataloaderConfig` and a `DatasetRuntimeContext`) that every entry point carries, serializes into `run_config.yaml`, and that the GPT dataset providers build their Megatron Core runtime config from, instead of re-reading the argparse namespace. First PR of the DatasetConfig series (follow-ups: TokenizerConfig authoritative, dataloader and batch consumers, `seq_length` ownership).

## Issue tracking

Linked issue: Related to #3554 (make `PretrainConfigContainer` authoritative), #6003 (load `run_config.yaml` into the container).

## Design

- **Declaration vs runtime object.** `megatron.core.datasets.gpt_dataset.GPTDatasetConfig` is a runtime object (asserts a built tokenizer, derives `split_matrix` / `token_dtype_code`, carries parallel sizes). The new `megatron.training.config.GPTDatasetConfig(MCoreGPTDatasetConfig, DataloaderConfig)` inherits its field names but holds what the user declared: no tokenizer, no file reads. `to_core_config(context)` builds a fresh Megatron Core config (or the existing runtime `GPTFIMDatasetConfig` for `dataset_type="fim"`) from the declaration plus a `DatasetRuntimeContext` (tokenizer, seed, parallel sizes, validation flags); the values Megatron Core derives and the defaults that depend on other fields (the legacy `split` when only `data_path` is given, `create_attention_mask` under inter-document masking, the SFT mock distribution from `seq_length`, `persistent_workers` with no workers) exist on the runtime object only and are never written back into the declaration. A declaration built from the CLI copies the validated `args`, which already carry the defaults `validate_args` materializes; a Python or YAML declaration gets them at conversion time. `megatron/core` is untouched.
- **Container lifecycle.** `validate()` is read-only and may run repeatedly (#6925); `finalize()` applies the spelling normalizations once, from `PretrainConfigContainer._finalize()` (`sequence_length` → `seq_length`, string `data_path` → list, phase transitions → sorted list, unset `dataloader_type` → `single`). `to_cfg_dict()` serializes that spelling-normalized declaration, so a reloaded `run_config.yaml` reacts to an edit of `seq_length`, `inter_document_masking` or `num_workers` like a fresh declaration, and it raises the `validate()` error for a declaration it cannot normalize instead of serializing a different, valid-looking one. Conversion and serialization are identical before and after finalization.
- **One family selector.** `dataset_type: Literal["gpt", "fim", "varlen", "sft"]` replaces the per-provider precedence over `--sft` / `--use-varlen-dataset` / `--fim-data`; the three flags stay as aliases of the new `--dataset-type`, and `validate_args` resolves the family once and writes it back into `args`, so both spellings drive the same checks, loaders and batches. An explicit value is accepted when it equals the aliases' legacy resolution (`sft` over `varlen` over `fim`, so `--dataset-type sft --sft --fim-data` is consistent); any other disagreement is an error, and `--sft --use-varlen-dataset` stays rejected. `mock_data` stays orthogonal.
- **Container threading.** `pretrain()` passes its container to `build_train_valid_test_data_iterators` → `build_train_valid_test_data_loaders` → `build_train_valid_test_datasets` (new keyword-only `cfg_container=None`, defaulting to the run config). A provider that declares `dataset_config` / `context` parameters receives `cfg.dataset` and the runtime context; every other provider, including ones taking `**kwargs`, is called exactly as before.
- **Per-entry-point policy.** `pretrain_gpt.py`, `pretrain_hybrid.py` and `pretrain_hybrid_flex.py` keep their own dataset-class tables and family-substitution rules (hybrid builds the gpt family for a fim request, flex for varlen and fim requests, each with a warning as before); `tools/prepare_cache.py` keeps its fixed GPT class and effective-config rule. Each passes the keywords its factory never forwarded through `to_core_config(exclude=...)` (unknown names are rejected), so the runtime object each builds is field-identical to the one it built before, over the tested matrix and with the three exceptions listed below. The four `core_gpt_dataset_config_from_args` functions remain as thin wrappers of the legacy call shape.

## Compatibility

| Surface | Status |
|---|---|
| CLI | Every legacy data flag keeps its spelling, dest, default, `nargs`, `type`, choices and action (snapshot test against the 48 legacy actions of `438ef0025`). New: `--dataset-type`, and the factory's `--disable-data-sharding` / `--disable-mmap-bin-files` spellings next to the existing `--no-*` ones. `--sample-rate` is parsed as before and warns that it has no effect. |
| `args` | Complete and normalized exactly as before; `validate_args` gains one call (selector projection) and one warning. Parser and `validate_args` check over the 347 functional-test `model_config.yaml` files (a parse / validation corpus, not an execution of the 347 cases; unknown flags are kept, not rejected): 308 validate on both `main` and this branch with every existing field equal, 39 fail identically on both (6 parse failures, list-valued flags the corpus tool does not expand; 33 `validate_args` assertions tied to the environment or the GPU count, mostly the FSDP `CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS` requirement and world-size divisibility), the only new field is `dataset_type`, and no declaration is rejected by `GPTDatasetConfig.validate()`. |
| Runtime dataset config | For each of the four entry points, type and field equality against frozen copies of the `438ef0025` factories and provider logic over 17 validated argument sets (blends, per-split, data-args files, mock, SFT, varlen, SBHD, FIM, cache flags, every forwarded knob, parallel inputs), subject to the three exceptions below, and sample equality for the mock builds that exist (`pretrain_gpt`: gpt, SFT and varlen mock; hybrid and flex: gpt and varlen mock). |
| Checkpoints | `run_config.yaml` gains a `dataset` section; files written before it load through `PretrainConfigContainer.from_dict/from_yaml(..., legacy_args=<validated namespace>)`, and are rejected with an explicit message without it. `check_checkpoint_args` unchanged. |
| Public signatures | Only optional parameters are added, keyword-only where they are new (`cfg_container=`, `dataset_config=` / `context=`, `legacy_args=`, `dataset_cfg=`); existing positions are preserved. The one deliberate change: constructing `PretrainConfigContainer` directly now requires `dataset=`; the two in-repo constructions (test fixture, RL config test) are updated. |
| `megatron/core` | Empty diff. |
| Megatron-Bridge | Bridge's container inherits `ConfigContainerBase`, whose `from_dict` / `from_yaml` gained the optional `legacy_args` hook here; Bridge's dataset implementations and its imports of Megatron-LM are untouched. Its selected unit tests give identical per-test outcomes on `438ef0025` and on this branch (below). |

Three documented behaviour differences, all intentional:

1. `--sft --fim-data` and `--use-varlen-dataset --fim-data` keep their dataset class and raw `validate_args` checks, but their runtime config is a plain `GPTDatasetConfig` instead of the `GPTFIMDatasetConfig` wrapper `pretrain_gpt` built around an SFT / varlen dataset. Tested: class and shared-field equality, an AST check that `sft_dataset.py` / `varlen_dataset.py` read no `fim_*` attribute, and identical mock SFT / varlen samples under the wrapper and the plain config. Real-data sample parity for these two combinations follows from those facts and is not demonstrated here (no local SFT / varlen fixture).
2. A declaration with no data source and no `--mock-data` now selects the mock dataset class where one exists (`pretrain_gpt`: gpt, SFT, varlen; hybrid: gpt, varlen; flex: gpt); the legacy providers keyed on `--mock-data` and paired a mock runtime config with the real dataset class, which failed to build.
3. `--mock-data` next to `--data-args-path` or `--per-split-data-args-path` (accepted by `validate_args`, which does not count file-backed sources) is rejected at container validation with the single-source message; the legacy GPT and hybrid providers paired `MockGPTDataset` with a runtime config resolved from the file (`mock=False`), which `MockGPTDataset` refuses, so the combination never trained (`tools/prepare_cache.py` rejects `--mock-data` itself). Two file-backed sources together are rejected the same way.

Scope boundary: dataset construction is migrated; the data loaders and batch functions still read `args` (`pin_memory`, `persistent_workers` and `drop_last` are accepted in YAML / Python but the existing loaders keep their built-in values until the consumer migration, next PR), and the parallel sizes and validation flags of the runtime context are still taken from `args` in `build_dataset_runtime_context` until their sections are authoritative.

## Commits

1. `refactor(training): add declarative GPTDatasetConfig and DataloaderConfig` (new module, class tests)
2. `refactor(training): add the dataset section to PretrainConfigContainer` (required section, runtime context, finalize hook, `legacy_args` upgrade, factories)
3. `refactor(training): generate the data argument group from GPTDatasetConfig` (`DatasetArgumentGroupFactory`, moved flags, selector projection, snapshot test)
4. `refactor(training): thread the config container to the dataset builders` (`training.py` plumbing, provider inspection)
5. `refactor(training): build GPT datasets from cfg.dataset in the providers` (four entry points, golden-equivalence tests)

## Test evidence

Local, two RTX A6000, `mlm-workstation:26.08-py3`, Megatron-LM `main` at `e8a302ac5` (the PR's base) as the baseline tree; every comparison below ran the same command on both trees.

- Unit, `torch.distributed.run --nproc-per-node 2` over `tests/unit_tests/training/`, `tests/unit_tests/test_training.py`, `tests/unit_tests/test_argument_utils.py` and `tests/unit_tests/data/{test_builder,test_gpt_dataset,test_fim_dataset,test_varlen_dataset,test_prepare_cache,test_data_samplers,test_get_batch}.py`: **1673 passed, 351 skipped, 6 failed, 9 deselected** (counts are per rank; both ranks run the same selection; skips are tests that need more than two GPUs). The 6 failures are the same 6 the same command gives on `e8a302ac5`: `test_fim_dataset.py::test_fim_gpt_dataset` (four parameter sets) and `test_full_dataset_length.py::test_cp_deduplicated_dataloader_length_reaches_every_rank` need the `/opt/data/tokenizers/huggingface` asset, and `test_initialization_lifecycle.py::test_rl_entrypoint_leaves_runtime_setup_to_pretrain` needs `uvicorn`, which the image lacks; `TestMegatronMLAArgumentGeneration` is deselected (needs `flash_mla`, fails on `main` too). Not a green suite in this environment; those are the only failures, and they match the baseline.
- New tests (collected cases): `tests/unit_tests/training/config/test_dataset_config.py` (84), `tests/unit_tests/training/test_dataset_ownership.py` (18), `test_data_arguments.py` (35: parser snapshot, end-to-end selector, docstring MRO), `test_dataset_providers.py` (92: golden equivalence against `legacy_dataset_factories.py`, mock builds, the three exceptions).
- Corpus check (parser and `validate_args` over the functional-test configs): 347 cases, 308 validated identically on both trees with every existing field equal, 39 matched failures (6 parse, 33 `validate_args`), 0 status mismatches, 0 declarations rejected by `GPTDatasetConfig.validate()`.
- Functional (mock data, `--deterministic-mode`, bf16, 20 iterations, seed 42, NullTokenizer; DP=2 and PP=2; `main` vs branch; legacy and `--dataset-type` spellings; save/restart vs uninterrupted). The gate is fail-fast and every comparison covers a declared iteration window on both sides, comparing every printed per-iteration metric (loss, learning rate, grad norm, params norm, consumed samples, skipped / nan counts): **all ten comparisons identical over their full windows (gate status 0): baseline repeatable; PR vs baseline for GPT, `--sft --mock-data`, `--use-varlen-dataset --mock-data` and PP=2 over iterations 1-20; `--dataset-type gpt|sft|varlen` vs the legacy spelling over 1-20; the run saved at iteration 10 vs the uninterrupted run over 1-10, and the restarted run over 11-20**. This establishes equality of the printed values at their printed precision, not full-precision parameter equality. The PR checkpoint's `run_config.yaml` carries the `dataset` section and round-trips through `from_yaml`; a baseline checkpoint's file upgrades with `legacy_args` and is rejected without it.
- Megatron-Bridge: Bridge `d86a5c09b`'s `tests/unit_tests/data` plus `training/test_config.py`, `test_train.py`, `test_pg_collection_wiring.py` and `test_log_non_default_values.py`, run in the training image with Bridge's sources on the path, once against `e8a302ac5` and once against this branch: **1350 passed, 182 failed, 3 skipped on both trees, and per test id 1350 passed / 1 skipped / 177 failed on both with 0 differing ids**. The failures are not introduced by this PR in this environment: same test ids, same outcome on the baseline. 171 of them are Bridge `d86a5c09b` running against a newer Megatron-LM than it pins (`DistributedInitConfig` no longer has `use_megatron_fsdp` since #7778, which fails `training/test_config.py` on both trees; against the PR's original base `438ef0025` the same run had 11 failures), and the remaining 11 are optional dependencies missing from the image (`process_vision_info` without `qwen_vl_utils`, `No module named 'diffusers'`).

## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests (existing `gpt` / `hybrid` functional suites cover the migrated providers; local mock-data runs above)
- [x] Not applicable: no GPU kernel is added or changed
- [x] I have added proper typing to my code
- [x] I have added relevant documentation (docstrings)
- [x] I have run `isort` on every edited file and `black` on the tests and the new module (`tools/autoformat.sh` scope)

+def dataset_type_from_args(args: Namespace, *, warn: bool = True) -> str:
+    """Resolve the dataset family from ``--dataset-type`` and the legacy alias flags.
+
+    The rule is stable under repetition, so ``validate_args`` (which writes the result back with
+    ``project_dataset_type_into_args``) and the config factories agree: an explicit ``dataset_type``
+    is consistent with alias flags when it equals their legacy resolution (``sft`` over ``varlen``
+    over ``fim``, as today's providers choose); any other disagreement is an error, a combination
+    that could not be written before. ``--sft`` with ``--use-varlen-dataset`` is rejected as
+    ``validate_args`` does. Several alias flags warn once (``warn=True``) where today the losers
+    are silently ignored.
+    """
+    explicit = getattr(args, "dataset_type", None)
+    aliases = [
+        family for _flag, (dest, family) in LEGACY_ALIAS_FLAGS.items() if getattr(args, dest, False)
+    ]
+    if "sft" in aliases and "varlen" in aliases:

+            "packed-sequence dataset family. Pick one."

+        raise ValueError(f"--dataset-type must be one of {DATASET_TYPES}, got {explicit!r}.")

+        raise ValueError(
+            f"--dataset-type {explicit} contradicts the legacy flag(s) selecting {aliases}."
+        )
+    if warn and len(aliases) > 1:
+        _warn(f"{aliases} were all requested; '{aliases[0]}' wins, as in today's providers.")
+    if explicit is not None:
+        return explicit
+    return legacy or "gpt"
